engines.name: TP400-D6

turboprop.rating_source: Ratings are certified: EASA TCDS E.033 Issue 08 (TP400-D6) normal take-off 7971 kW, uprated take-off 8251 kW, maximum continuous 7971 kW (sea level ISA, test-bed installation, no bleed or offtake); reduction ratio 9.929:1 from the same TCDS. ESTIMATES, not published: maximum climb and maximum cruise shaft power are the PW127M catalogue fractions of normal take-off power (1634.574/1845.607 = 0.88566 and 1589.832/1845.607 = 0.86141) applied to 7971 kW; maximum_cruise_fuel_flow_kg_h is a TWO-engine figure (FUEL_FLOW_REFERENCE_ENGINES = 2) equal to 2 x the PW127M power-specific fuel consumption (762/2 kg/h over 1589.832 kW = 0.23965 kg/kWh) x 6866.3 kW; no TP400-D6 SFC or climb/cruise rating is public. 1 shp = 0.745699872 kW
turboprop.geometry_source: EASA TCDS P.012 Issue 04 (Ratier-Figeac FH385/FH386): diameter 5.334 m, 8 blades, 860 rpm take-off, 842 rpm maximum continuous; propeller speed 860 rpm is the governed take-off value

engines.cycle_anchor_source: EASA TCDS E.033 Issue 08; climb/cruise power and fuel flow are PW127M-fraction estimates (see rating_source)

engines.geometry_source: ESTIMATE: nacelle length 5.5 m and radius 1.1 m are not published; EASA TCDS E.033 gives engine length 4.180 m (PGB front to nozzle) and maximum radius 1.218 m from the centre line at the lowest point
